Independent re-read of the original page images: (1) p8 Fig. 5 panel 'Yield (kg plant-1)' (receipt SRC-12bc559a15bfa19a765d321a): Drought bar ~0.19 (letter e) and AC + Drought bar ~0.81 (letter d) on axis 0.0/0.5/1.0/1.5, caption 'mean +/- standard error (SE) of three replications (n = 3)'; stored means 0.1924 (tv 255) and 0.8104 (tv 251) match the rendered bars. (2) p9 Results text (receipt SRC-e52a9a984fdcde8d8f506244) prints per-plant yield 1.17 kg (well-watered) to 0.19 kg (drought), 'an 83.8% reduction', and AC 0.81 kg plant-1; printed-mean lnRR = ln(0.81/0.19) = 1.450, within 0.012 of the stored figure-based 1.438 (difference driven by digitized drought mean 0.1924 vs printed 0.19, 1.2%), so the outlier status is not a digitization artefact. (3) p1 Abstract (receipt SRC-515bf263aba54b152eb8d2a6) repeats AC yield 0.81 kg plant-1. (4) p3 Methods 'Assessment of yield parameters' (receipt SRC-d1f66da82589f3b9e3fa119b): yield per plant (kg plant-1) = sum of weights of all fruits harvested from each plant, three biological replicates per treatment; unit, organ, denominator and cumulative harvest window match the stored signature. Internal consistency: fruits per plant fall from 24.39 to 7.73 under drought and recover to 16.73 with AC (p9), consistent with the very low drought-control yield. The extreme lnRR arises from the severe drought penalty on the shared drought control (E1.S, 0.19 kg/plant), not from an identity, unit, arm-mapping or transcription error. Shared control E1.S is common to the four SB_vs_S yield contrasts (issues 4399-4402) and is already recorded via shared_control_id and dependency cluster DC-T077. Existing flag ERROR_BAR_DIGITIZATION_OVER_5PCT concerns the SE bars, not the means, and is unaffected.

BIOTIC_PATHOGEN_LOAD MD=0.146 is a robust outlier (|z_MAD|=9.5 > 4.5) — review, never delete
resolution: Contrast 81873f2bf5c8a7aee9d497f4 (E1.SB_Z13 vs E1.S, TSWV DAS-ELISA OD415, apical non-inoculated leaf, 20 dpi, MD = 1.4376 - 1.2911 = 0.146, flag BOX_CENTRE_ASSUMED_MEAN) was re-checked independently in the original. Page 6 Figure 2C was rendered at 300 dpi (receipt SRC-49e9ee8599173bed11fa2f07). The linear y axis has labelled ticks 0, 0.5, 1.0, 1.5 and 2.0. The Water (red, first) box centre line sits just below 1.3 (about 1.29) and the Z13 (light blue, second) centre line sits just below 1.45 (about 1.43-1.44). Both independent readings agree with the stored values (tv 1967 = 1.291, tv 1966 = 1.438) well within the 5% tolerance. Z13 is visibly the highest box in the panel, with points up to about 1.9 OD. The caption (p6) says there was no significant difference among treatments. The Results text on p5 (receipt SRC-4ed4e5c79692588166c0ed77) independently supports the direction and size: 'a non-significant trend towards higher OD415 values (p = 0.08) was recorded upon Z13 application (mean OD415 1.4 +/- 0.24)', against EP3 'mean OD415 1.29 +/- 0.18'. The printed Z13 mean of 1.4 is consistent with the 1.44 box centre. No arm, axis, timepoint, unit or transcription error was found. The robust z score is high (|z_MAD| = 9.5) because the comparison set of MD pathogen-load contrasts is small and the other T081 box-centre MDs cluster tightly near zero (-0.03 to 0.13), which gives a tiny MAD. The 0.146 OD difference is a genuine, source-supported value. It is retained unchanged and flagged; it is not deleted or winsorized. Limitations stay attached: the box centre is used as a mean only under the project assumption BOX_CENTRE_ASSUMED_MEAN (the authors do not define the centre statistic), there is no variance (whiskers and boxes are not SD/SE; var_available = 0), and n = 30 plants per treatment comes from Methods p4.

message: BIOTIC_SEVERITY MD=-3.670 is a robust outlier (|z_MAD|=5.0 > 4.5) — review, never delete
resolution: Contrast 5a17f4a1929b881ed5ec6bc6 (E2 Xep bacterial spot, SB_vs_S, E2.SB.S54 vs E2.S, BIOTIC_SEVERITY MD=-3.67) re-read in the original PDF page 15 image, Table 5, Xep column 'Disease severity c' (footnote c: percent leaf area affected by bacterial spot): row 'Paenarthrobacter ureafaciens S54' = 11.28 ab; row 'Control' = 14.95 a. 11.28 - 14.95 = -3.67, matching mean_t/mean_c/effect exactly. Internal consistency check: the printed Biocontrol efficacy (%) d for S54 = 24.50, and (14.95-11.28)/14.95 = 24.55% (rounding of printed means), confirming the cell identity and row alignment. The Tukey letters (S54 'ab' shares 'a' with Control) show S54 is genuinely the weakest Xep severity reduction among the 10 strains (other strains 1.55-8.31, i.e. MD about -6.6 to -13.4), so the robust-z outlier reflects a true small effect relative to the study-wide distribution, not a transcription, unit, arm or timepoint error. Unit (% leaf area), arm, 6 dpi timepoint and n=6 plants per arm are consistent with the slot T024#06 definition. No correction needed; retain value unchanged with outlier flag (no deletion, no winsorization). var_effect remains unavailable because Table 5 prints no SD/SE.

message: BIOTIC_SEVERITY lnRR=-2.166 is a robust outlier (|z_MAD|=5.4 > 4.5) — review, never delete
resolution: Contrast fd2d2babe0c0e3f0bb026d3e (BIOTIC_SEVERITY, context FIG7B_BROWNING_SPOT_COUNT, TP_D70, T6 = 500 mg/L ZnO-NPs [E1.S.ZnONP500] vs TO+ inoculated control [E1.S]; mean_t 0.778, mean_c 6.782, lnRR -2.166). I re-read the original PDF p13 Figure 7b myself (receipt SRC-67d9625e089c885389160515, 300 dpi). The blue-violet 'No. of browning spots' bar for TO+ is the second-tallest bar in the panel, at about 6.8 on the 0-12 axis (ticks every 2), with an upper SE cap near 9.7 and letter 'a'. The T6 browning-spot bar is the smallest bar in the panel, at about 0.8, with a cap near 1.2 and letter 'b'. The digitized means (6.78 and 0.78) agree with my independent visual reading, so the ratio of about 0.115 (lnRR about -2.17) is a real feature of the source data. The extreme value comes from a near-zero treated count against a high inoculated-control count. It is not an identity, arm, unit or transcription error. The contrast is within one study and one figure series, with a shared control and a common background. I also re-read the p9 prose (receipt SRC-3ee99f949591d20481a472a0). It prints no TO+ browning-spot value. For T6 it says '1.00 browning spots, 2.4 yellowed branches, and 0.80 yellowed leaves'. In the Fig. 7b T6 group, the orange yellowing-branch bar is about 1.0, the purple browning-spot bar about 0.8 and the pink yellowing-leaf bar about 2.4. So the prose appears to permute the series labels. Under the binding figure-over-prose rule, the figure value of about 0.8 stays. Even the prose value of 1.00 would give lnRR of about -1.91, which is still a large reduction, so the outlier status does not depend on this discrepancy. The T6 mean resolution bound is 3.3%, within the 5% limit. Its upper error bar keeps the existing ERROR_BAR_DIGITIZATION_OVER_5PCT flag (13% geometric bound), which affects variance precision, not the mean. Error bars are SE per Sec. 2.8, with n = 3 pots of 5 plants. The denominator for the count is not printed (UNSPECIFIED); this is a known limitation that is already carried in unit_raw. Decision: retain the contrast unchanged with the outlier flag as a genuine biological or measurement extreme. Do not delete, winsorize or alter it. No correction is required.

message: DRY_BIOMASS lnRR=1.885 is a robust outlier (|z_MAD|=4.5 > 4.5) — review, never delete
resolution: Genuine outlier from the source; keep it unchanged, no deletion or winsorizing. Contrast db20dcc13c74e6755078cef6 (SB_vs_S, E1, root dry biomass, E1.SB SA/S vs E1.S WSA/S, tp E1.T15, unit bare g) has mean_t=2.465, mean_c=0.374, lnRR=1.885. I re-read the original PDF page 5 at 300 dpi myself (receipt SRC-5693381cc1a77a0c697509a3). Fig. 1f 'Root dry weight (g)' y-axis runs 0-5 with ticks 0,1,2,3,4,5 (~59.6 display px per g). The SA/S bar top sits at ~2.45 g (letter d) and the WSA/S bar top at ~0.37 g (letter c), with an upper SD cap at ~0.60 g (SD ~0.23). Both match the stored values within graphical tolerance. The caption says these are means of three replicates with SD error bars, which matches n=3 and SD in the contrast. The two bars carry different significance letters (c vs d), so the authors report a significant difference. The large ratio (~6.6x, +559%) comes from a very small salt-stressed non-inoculated root dry weight and matches the photo in Fig. 1b (a much smaller WSA/S root). It is not an extraction, unit, arm-identity or sign error. The arm labels WSA/S and SA/S are taken from the caption legend. The contrast keeps its existing caveats: (i) root-only dry biomass, kept separate from shoot/whole-plant; (ii) bare g with no printed denominator; (iii) the ERROR_BAR_DIGITIZATION_OVER_5PCT flag, because the small WSA/S bar's SD gives high relative digitization uncertainty; (iv) shared control T044|E1|E1.S within dependency cluster DC-T044. The C001 robust-outlier flag should stay visible for sensitivity analyses.
